comments.story: Apple headset leak reveals new details and confirms earlier rumors
comments.why: Starline suggests video calls could become a completely different experience.
comments.text: We might just not know what we are missing. I used to think that video calls is a solved problem until I saw Google's Project Starline [0]. Video calls in AR could be vastly better, not just a little bit, but basically a completely different experience/relationship. [0] [VIDEO]

comments.author: esafak
comments.story: We need technology that is less immersive, not more
comments.why: Tech demo showing user reactions to photorealistic calls.
comments.text: This is true of games, but not other applications. You need photorealism to have immersive video calls -- as if you are meeting in person. Here is a tech demo by Google; see how users respond to the realism: [VIDEO] So we do need more immersive technology; just maybe not for games.

comments.author: achow
comments.story: Project Starline: Feel like you're there, together
comments.why: Notes the demo conspicuously avoids showing participants touching the glass.
comments.text: If you watch the video of it: [VIDEO] Interesting thing to note is that they don't show the participants touching the glass pane 'separating' them, whereas for that kind of situation it would be very very natural thing to do. I guess doing so (reaching towards the 'glass pane') would make the imagery distort/degrade real fast as you would start going out of camera's FoV, which that would break the magic.
